description:
FILED s458al (agent AL, round 15), found by the #840 probes when the REAL
perl experimental.pm started loading under PCL.

lib/version.pm's overloaded `<=>` / `cmp` is `sub vcmp { ... return $a cmp $b }`
-- a plain STRING comparison of the two version STRINGS.  perl's
version::vcmp normalises both sides into component tuples first:

  a DECIMAL string  "5.030000" -> integer part, then the fraction in 3-digit
                    groups                       -> v5.30.0
  a DOTTED string   "5.14.0"   -> the dot-separated parts
                                               -> v5.14.0

and compares componentwise, missing components 0.

PROBE (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl, both on the same file):

    use version ();
    my $v = version->new('5.14.0');
    my $w = version->new('5.30.0');
    print "] < v : ", ($] < $v ? 1 : 0), "\n";   # perl 0   PCL 1
    print "] >= w : ", ($] >= $w ? 1 : 0), "\n"; # perl 1   PCL 0
    print "cmp   : ", ($] <=> $v), "\n";         # perl 1   PCL -1
    print "numify: ", $v->numify, "\n";          # perl 5.014000  PCL 5.14

TWO bugs in one probe, and note the SECOND is a different variable:

  (a) vcmp compares strings.  "5.030000" cmp "5.14.0" is -1 because "5.0"
      sorts before "5.1"; as VERSIONS 5.30.0 > 5.14.0.  Every `$version <
      5.010` / `>= 5.008` idiom in CPAN code is at risk, and the answer is
      silent.
  (b) numify returns `$s + 0` (5.14), where perl returns the normalised
      decimal 5.014000.  Same normalisation, so one helper fixes both.

REACHED BY: the real experimental.pm's last two _enable arms.  Measured after
#840 deleted the shim -- `use experimental 'autoderef'` croaks "Need perl
5.14.0 or later for feature autoderef" where perl croaks "Experimental
feature autoderef has been removed from perl in version 5.24.0", and
`use experimental 'array_base'` does not croak at all where perl does.  Both
are strictly closer to perl than the deleted shim's "accept everything", so
they did not block #840.

RELATED, and NOT the same task: PCL reports `$]` = 5.030000 and `$^V` =
v5.30.0 (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp lines 1213-1214, 2082), while the project
targets perl 5.40 semantics everywhere else (the #360 feature table, the
5.40 bundles, this task's tables).  A program that branches on `$]` gets
5.30's answer.  Deliberate or stale is not established -- raising the claim
touches `%p-parse-require-version` (`use v5.36;` must keep working) and any
test that branches on the version, so it wants its own measurement.  Task
#871.

BAR: the four probe lines above identical to perl, plus perl's own
t/op/packagev.t and the version-comparison rows of the companion suite; a
lib/ change makes the full sweep non-optional.


DONE s459an (agent AN, round 16).  ONE _parse feeds vcmp/numify/normal/is_qv/is_alpha; a decimal fraction cuts into 3-digit groups right-padded, a dotted version (leading v OR two-plus dots) splits and pads to three, missing components 0.  MEASURED, do not re-derive: the alpha `_` is REMOVED on BOTH paths -- treating it as a component separator in the dotted form is wrong by 24 rows (v1.2_3 is v1.23.0, 1.2.3_4 is v1.2.34).  Validated 3864 checks over 56 strings vs the REAL version:: (perl 5.40.3), under perl AND under PCL; experimental.pm's two croaks now byte-identical.  Guard Pl/t/version-shim-01.t 2 -> 4 rows, inverse-verified against the base shim.  NOTE the task's four probe lines need PCL_NO_RAW_VERDICT=1 on main because of #890 (an overloaded object from a MODULE dies under the raw-numeric freeze) -- filed, not this task's bug; the no-temporary spelling runs in default mode.  vcmp negates rather than swapping its two tuples because (($x,$y)=($y,$x)) on refs is silently wrong today -- #891.
subject: lib/version.pm's vcmp is a STRING compare -- `$] < version->new('5.14.0')` is TRUE under PCL (silent wrong)
